script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The line about grumbling at dinner invents a scene and implies the brothers grumbled there.
The final sentence comments on the fill-in-the-blank question itself.
The text says Jephthah was denied an inheritance, not that he lost land he already possessed.
Calling the men 'interesting company' adds Papa Dorin's own comment to the text's harsh description of a group.
The text does not establish that no priest was present.
The text does not identify the men's origins or establish that none were Edomite soldiers. Edom also appears when Israel bypasses its land, not only in the request to its king.
The text does not say the elders let Jephthah be driven out. Jephthah tells them they expelled him.
The text does not say what the elders thought of Jephthah's valor.
The text does not say whether Jephthah smiled when he spoke.
The explanation states Jephthah's thoughts as fact, including what he was not thinking about.
Saying he asks before any swords come out invents a detail and overlooks that the Ammonites are already at war with Israel.
The explanation is flat and repeats the question's answer without adding a distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
Saying Jephthah does not offer a truce 'yet' implies that he offers one later.
The explanation is generic and simply repeats the king's demand.
The claim that there would have been no long way around if both kings had agreed is an unmarked speculation about what would have happened.
The text specifies the land of the Amorites who inhabited that country. 'All the land of the Amorites' leaves out that qualification.
The text does not establish that nobody stepped in between the sides.
The king's recorded message does not say what Jephthah says about Chemosh.
Jephthah asks the king a question about what Chemosh grants; the explanation turns it into an assertion.
The text does not say the complaint had been met with silence for three hundred years. Jephthah asks why the cities were not taken back during that time.
The explanation is flat and repeats the number without developing the point Jephthah makes with it.
The claim that Shepherd is a title for the LORD elsewhere in Scripture needs a reference to that passage.
The text says the king paid no heed to the message; it does not say he heard the whole case.
